notes: Canonical capability manifest (Contract A). Every stat, card, pill, drawer and search hit on the portal derives from this file. Maturity is stable | experimental | roadmap. Outcomes use exactly the five developer lenses. featured_top12 marks the twelve flagship pillars (Contract B).

outcomeDescriptions.build-verify: Scope with /po, run the governed pipeline, collect Speculative Shadow Evidence and close with a Result Ledger and /ship.
outcomeDescriptions.parallel-runs: Linked worktrees under /runs, live mux panes in tmux/zellij/wezterm, Council Mode and quota-reset parking.
outcomeDescriptions.mobile-remote: Drive iOS and Android from .axym/mobile.json: /sim, /device visual diff, /qa --maestro, /security --masvs, /bg and LAN pairing.
outcomeDescriptions.security-firewall: Local MCP capability-lattice firewall, adversarial QA passes, Web posture checks and the headless axym fitness CI gate.
outcomeDescriptions.context-runtime: Living Repo Brain and prompt-cache telemetry, LinUCB cost routing, offline replay, Calm-UX resilience and cross-surface continuity.

capabilities.name: One session, any agent CLI
capabilities.summary: Drive Claude, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode and more from one consistent interface.
capabilities.search: claude codex gemini opencode cursor copilot keyless provider cli interface failover
capabilities.problem: Every agent CLI ships its own interface, so switching models means re-learning a tool and losing the thread mid-problem.
capabilities.what_it_is: One terminal session that drives Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor Agent, GitHub Copilot CLI and Antigravity through a single consistent interface with zero static API keys.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You keep one conversation and one set of habits while choosing the model that fits the task — credentials stay with each CLI, never with Axym.
capabilities.limitations: Provider coverage depends on the CLIs installed on your PATH; a provider that is not installed is listed as 'not found' by axym doctor.

capabilities.name: Provider discovery and defaults
capabilities.summary: Setup is detection, not configuration — installed CLIs are found automatically.
capabilities.search: doctor detection install path alias typo defaults config
capabilities.what_it_is: Finds installed CLIs on PATH and in common install directories, accepts ids, aliases and display names, and suggests the closest match on a typo.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Setup stays a detection step, not a config-file exercise: Axym finds what you installed and suggests the closest match when you mistype an id.
capabilities.limitations: Private or uncommonly located CLIs may need a one-time registration in ~/.axym/providers.json.

capabilities.name: Mid-session provider & model switching
capabilities.summary: Swap provider, model or reasoning effort mid-problem. The thread never drops.
capabilities.search: switch provider model effort mid-session reasoning
capabilities.what_it_is: Change the agent, model or reasoning effort without losing the conversation or restarting the session.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A provider that is wrong for one step no longer costs the conversation — you switch and continue with the same context.
capabilities.limitations: Model availability differs per provider CLI; the picker lists what the selected CLI actually exposes.

capabilities.name: Automatic failover & cooldowns
capabilities.summary: A quota wall benches that provider; the run continues somewhere else.
capabilities.search: failover cooldown quota circuit breaker bench reset
capabilities.what_it_is: Classifies failures as immediate, after-reset or never; benches quota walls until their reset time and policy walls for 24h; a circuit breaker stops repeated sub-minute failures.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A quota wall or flaky CLI no longer ends the run: the failure is classified, the provider is benched until reset, and the next provider receives a handoff.
capabilities.use_it: Automatic on a failed turn · /priority shows the resolution order
capabilities.limitations: Failover quality depends on how many provider CLIs are installed; with a single CLI there is nowhere to fail over to.

capabilities.name: Persistent Claude connection
capabilities.summary: A live stream-JSON process, so repeat turns start instantly.
capabilities.search: claude stream-json persistent connection stdin permissions fast
capabilities.what_it_is: Claude runs as a long-lived stream-JSON process, so repeat turns skip CLI re-initialisation and permission requests flow over live stdin.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Repeat turns skip CLI startup, so interactive work stays immediate and permission prompts flow over the live connection.
capabilities.limitations: Applies to the Claude provider only; other CLIs are invoked per turn.

capabilities.name: Sessions, resume & reconciliation
capabilities.summary: Come back tomorrow — it restores the session and reports what changed.
capabilities.search: resume continue session jsonl git reconciliation workspace changed
capabilities.what_it_is: Saves every finished turn as JSONL, restores the provider's own session id, and tells you what changed in the workspace since the session was last active.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Coming back later is safe: the provider's own session id is restored and you are told what changed in the workspace while you were away.
capabilities.limitations: Provider-side session retention policies still apply; very old provider sessions may no longer be restorable by the CLI itself.

capabilities.name: Self-healing doctor & onboarding
capabilities.summary: A 30-second, non-destructive setup that detects providers and repairs common problems itself.
capabilities.search: doctor self-healing onboarding 30 seconds repair scar rules block recurring non-destructive
capabilities.what_it_is: A non-destructive onboarding path: axym doctor detects installed agent CLIs, verifies the runtime, repairs common setup problems itself, and locally verified scar rules can block edits that already failed the same way before.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Setup stays a detection step that can heal itself, and mistakes the organisation has already made once are not repeated silently.
capabilities.limitations: Repairs are limited to known, safe setup fixes; anything destructive is reported, never attempted.

capabilities.name: Multi-account provider slots
capabilities.summary: Switch personal, work and sandbox accounts per provider with trust zones and kernel isolation.
capabilities.search: accounts multi-account slots personal work sandbox trust zone pinned seatbelt landlock canary isolation cooldown
capabilities.what_it_is: Configure and switch between multiple accounts per provider (personal, work, sandbox) with trust-zone policies, pinned-account enforcement, per-account health and cooldown tracking, and kernel-isolated credential directories (macOS Seatbelt / Linux Landlock) with egress-proxy canary protection.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You can keep personal, client and sandbox credentials strictly separated — when one account hits a rate limit or trust-zone rule, Axym never leaks credentials across slots.
capabilities.limitations: Kernel isolation uses macOS Seatbelt and Linux Landlock; Windows credential directories are isolated by path but not by an OS sandbox.

capabilities.name: OpenAI-compatible local inference
capabilities.summary: Drive Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM or llama.cpp through the same TUI session and Result Ledger.
capabilities.search: local openai-compatible ollama lm studio vllm llama.cpp self-hosted model air-gapped
capabilities.what_it_is: Connect local or self-hosted OpenAI-compatible inference servers (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp) through the same TUI session, tool loop and Result Ledger with no cloud CLI required.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Air-gapped, private or local-GPU workflows get the exact same permissions, diffing and verification harness as cloud CLIs.
capabilities.limitations: Tool-calling fidelity varies by local server; features that need native provider modes (e.g. Claude stream-json permissions) do not apply.

capabilities.name: Session outcome profiles
capabilities.summary: Shape turn evaluation with session-scoped verification, speed or audit profiles.
capabilities.search: profile outcome strict prototype security audit quality preset
capabilities.what_it_is: Select a session-scoped outcome profile (such as strict verification, rapid prototype or security audit) that shapes how turns are evaluated.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You can dial up verification rigor for production changes or speed for exploration without editing config files.
capabilities.limitations: Profiles shape evaluation and defaults; they never weaken approval gates.

capabilities.name: Streaming chat & tool activity
capabilities.summary: Watch real commands, paths and output while the agent works.
capabilities.search: streaming tokens tool calls markdown live output
capabilities.what_it_is: Token-level deltas, lightweight markdown and animated tool calls with real commands, paths and outputs instead of raw protocol dumps.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You see real commands, paths and outputs as they happen, so you can intervene before a wrong assumption becomes a committed change.
capabilities.limitations: Rendering fidelity follows the provider's stream format; raw protocol dumps are summarised, not hidden.

capabilities.name: Result Ledger
capabilities.summary: Every turn ends with a receipt: outcome, files, checks, blockers.
capabilities.search: result ledger outcome ok fail ver unv files checks blockers
capabilities.what_it_is: Each turn ends with an outcome banner (OK, FAIL, VER, UNV), modified files, verification checks, blockers or risks, a concise summary and contextual next actions.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A turn ends with an inspectable outcome instead of a vibe — files touched, checks run, blockers and next actions are explicit.
capabilities.use_it: Automatic at turn completion · Ctrl+O expands detail
capabilities.limitations: Unverified dimensions are marked UNV; the ledger never scores unmeasured work as perfect.

capabilities.name: Markdown & syntax highlighting
capabilities.summary: Answers render as documents and code as code — no external dependency.
capabilities.search: markdown syntax highlighting code fence rust go python shell yaml
capabilities.what_it_is: Fenced code is highlighted for JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Rust, Go, shell, YAML/TOML and C-family languages with no external dependency.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Code in the terminal is scannable without a separate viewer or an external highlighting dependency.
capabilities.limitations: Very long fenced blocks collapse for scroll performance; expand with Ctrl+O.

capabilities.name: Message queueing
capabilities.summary: Keep typing while it works — instructions drain in order, never lost.
capabilities.search: queue message typing busy drain order workstream
capabilities.what_it_is: Text submitted while a turn is running is queued and drains automatically when the turn ends, with a visible queued count. Governed workstream submissions are the exception: they are refused while the runtime is busy and can be retried when it is idle.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You can keep typing while the agent works; the next instruction is queued and drains in order instead of being lost to a busy turn. Governed work is never silently stacked behind another turn.
capabilities.use_it: Type while the agent is working
capabilities.limitations: Governed workstreams deliberately refuse submission while a run is busy instead of queueing behind it.

capabilities.name: Transcript search & turn jump
capabilities.summary: Find any decision and jump straight back to the turn that made it.
capabilities.search: find search transcript jump turns ctrl+f export saved
capabilities.what_it_is: Search the current session, open a scrollable hit preview, or jump directly to an earlier conversational turn.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Long sessions stay navigable: find a decision by text and jump straight back to the turn where it was made.
capabilities.limitations: Search covers the current session transcript; use /handoff export to carry context to a new session.

capabilities.name: Copy and export
capabilities.summary: Lift one answer or the whole transcript into a ticket or PR.
capabilities.search: copy export clipboard markdown transcript ticket pr
capabilities.what_it_is: Copy the latest or an earlier response to the system clipboard, or save the full transcript as markdown.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Results move into a note, ticket or PR without retyping, and the whole transcript can be kept as markdown.
capabilities.limitations: Exports are local files; nothing is uploaded anywhere.

capabilities.name: Calm status & retry collapse
capabilities.summary: One in-place live status row instead of scrollback noise; retries collapse to a quiet line.
capabilities.search: calm status row retry collapse scrollback quiet expandable in-place live calm-ux
capabilities.what_it_is: One in-place live status row replaces appended pause markers, and transient retries that recover on their own collapse into a single quiet, expandable line instead of a stack of scrollback.
capabilities.why_it_matters: The transcript stays readable during long, flaky turns: you see current state at a glance and can expand the history only if you care.
capabilities.limitations: Collapsed retries remain expandable in place; the full history is never deleted.

capabilities.name: Multi-line composer
capabilities.summary: Readline keys your fingers already know — motion, kill/yank, undo.
capabilities.search: readline multi-line newline ctrl+a e u k w kill yank undo history footer
capabilities.what_it_is: Cursor motion, word jump, kill/yank, undo, history navigation and a hinted footer work across single-line and multi-line input.
capabilities.why_it_matters: The composer behaves like an editor, so long prompts and pasted context are comfortable to shape in a terminal.
capabilities.use_it: Shift+Enter or Ctrl+J for a newline · Ctrl+A/E/U/K/W for editing
capabilities.limitations: Key handling follows standard readline conventions; terminal-specific key reporting gaps may remap a few chords.

capabilities.name: Vim mode & external editor
capabilities.summary: Compose in Vim bindings, or open the prompt in $EDITOR.
capabilities.search: vim external editor visual editor ctrl+g keybindings
capabilities.what_it_is: Persistent Vim keybindings for the prompt, or open the current prompt in your own $VISUAL/$EDITOR.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Your existing editing muscle memory works in the prompt, and $EDITOR handles anything you would rather write in a full editor.
capabilities.limitations: Vim mode covers the composer, not the whole interface.

capabilities.name: @file completion
capabilities.summary: Attach any file with a fuzzy @ mention — a few keystrokes, not a path.
capabilities.search: @file completion fuzzy attach path git ls-files
capabilities.what_it_is: Fuzzy-complete project files from git ls-files, or a bounded directory walk outside git, ranked by filename, path and subsequence match.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Attaching the right file is a few keystrokes instead of a path you have to remember or paste.
capabilities.use_it: Type @ followed by part of a path
capabilities.limitations: Outside git, the directory walk is deliberately bounded; very large untracked trees may need an explicit path.

capabilities.name: Prompt history & reverse search
capabilities.summary: Your last 500 prompts, searchable — good prompts stay reusable.
capabilities.search: history reverse search 500 prompts ctrl+r regex
capabilities.what_it_is: Keeps the last 500 prompts and offers bash-style reverse search over them.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Useful prompts stay reusable; reverse search finds them without scrolling the transcript.
capabilities.limitations: History is local to your machine and capped at the last 500 prompts.

capabilities.name: Paste formatting & images
capabilities.summary: Screenshots and big pastes become structured inputs the model can use.
capabilities.search: paste image screenshot attach clipboard format collapsible ctrl+i
capabilities.what_it_is: Formats large pasted text into a collapsible prompt, and attaches screenshots or image files as [Image #n] inputs.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Large pastes and screenshots become structured inputs the provider can actually use, rather than a wall of text.
capabilities.limitations: Image support depends on the provider CLI accepting image inputs; terminal graphics support is probed with /termcaps.

capabilities.name: Plan, Ask, Edit & Auto modes
capabilities.summary: Four dials of freedom, one keystroke apart. Start in Plan.
capabilities.search: plan ask edit auto permission mode shift+tab read-only yolo
capabilities.what_it_is: Plan is read-only, Ask never edits, Edit auto-accepts file edits, and Auto bypasses permission prompts; each maps to the provider's native permission mode.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You choose how much authority the agent has for this task with a visible mode, not an implicit trust decision.
capabilities.limitations: Governed runtime approval gates are never bypassed, even in Auto.

capabilities.name: Inline permission gate
capabilities.summary: Risky commands pause and show themselves before they run.
capabilities.search: permission gate allow deny command path relay y n default deny
capabilities.what_it_is: Permission-requiring tool calls are relayed to the TUI and answered there: allow or deny with the real command or path shown. Gate errors and interrupts deny by default.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Dangerous commands are decided where you are, with the real command shown; errors and interrupts deny by default.
capabilities.use_it: Answer y or n when a gate appears · AXYM_TUI_NO_RELAY=1 opts out
capabilities.limitations: Gate prompts are answered by the person at the terminal; remote surfaces get the same gates only when paired with scoped access.

capabilities.name: Always-allow command list
capabilities.summary: Pre-approve exact commands you trust; everything else still asks.
capabilities.search: always allow permissions list exact review clear trust
capabilities.what_it_is: Review or clear exact commands you have chosen to always allow, so repeated safe commands stop asking.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Repeated safe commands stop interrupting you, while the list stays reviewable and exact instead of becoming a blanket bypass.
capabilities.limitations: Matches are exact strings, not globs — a changed command asks again.

capabilities.name: Explicit YOLO mode
capabilities.summary: Full autonomy exists — you must ask for it by name.
capabilities.search: yolo explicit risk auto sandbox governed gates never bypassed
capabilities.what_it_is: Skips every approval prompt and implies Auto mode, with the risk stated up front. Governed runtime approval gates are never bypassed.
capabilities.why_it_matters: For disposable sandboxes you can opt into speed explicitly, with the risk stated up front and governed runtime gates still intact.
capabilities.limitations: Not recommended outside disposable sandboxes; governed runtime gates still apply.

capabilities.name: Crash-safe terminal handling
capabilities.summary: A crash never leaves a garbled terminal or a stuck wake-lock.
capabilities.search: crash safe terminal render raw mode wake lock signal garbled
capabilities.what_it_is: A render error or external signal unmounts cleanly, restores raw-mode terminal state, and releases the wake-lock child instead of leaving a garbled screen.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A crash or signal restores the terminal instead of leaving a garbled screen and a held wake lock.
capabilities.limitations: Restoration covers Axym-owned terminal state; state changed by other processes cannot be repaired.

capabilities.name: Anti-hang guard
capabilities.summary: A hung tool call is classified, drained and escalated — it can never wedge the session.
capabilities.search: anti-hang guard calm-ux hung tool prompt killer lock classifier orphan drain stall escalation circuit breaker linucb cost router failover
capabilities.problem: Silent hangs and runaway retry loops burn tokens and terminal patience — the session looks alive while nothing progresses.
capabilities.what_it_is: The Calm-UX layer: tool calls run in a non-interactive command environment with a prompt killer, a lock classifier, an orphan drain and verified-idle process-group escalation, surfacing as a typed ToolStallError instead of a silent hang — alongside an identical-failure circuit breaker and, on the daemon, LinUCB cost/failover routing that moves work off a stalling provider.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A hung tool call is classified, drained and escalated — it can never wedge the session, loop on the same failure, or burn quota on a provider that stopped answering.
capabilities.use_it: Automatic · pair with AXYM_AUTO_ROUTE=cost on axym serve for cost-aware failover
capabilities.limitations: Cost routing (LinUCB + economic governor) needs the axym serve daemon; in a plain TUI session the anti-hang and circuit-breaker guards apply but routing decisions stay manual.

capabilities.name: Identical-failure circuit breaker
capabilities.summary: Stops repeated identical tool failures and offers a clean, visible way forward.
capabilities.search: identical failure circuit breaker tool loop repeat question footer bypass autonomous
capabilities.what_it_is: A tool-loop breaker detects repeated identical failures and stops them, offering a native question footer with a clean, explicit autonomous bypass.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Repeating the same failing action cannot burn tokens in a loop; the way forward is always a visible decision, not a crash.
capabilities.limitations: Near-identical failures with cosmetic differences are not collapsed; the breaker keys on repeated identical failures.

capabilities.name: Adaptive workspaces
capabilities.summary: The interface reshapes itself for the job: explore, execute, review, approve.
capabilities.search: workspace adaptive explore execute investigate review approval hints header
capabilities.what_it_is: Switch the session between explore, execute, investigate, review and approval modes so the header, hints and available actions match the job.
capabilities.why_it_matters: The interface matches the job — exploring, implementing, investigating, reviewing or approving — so the relevant actions are near at hand.
capabilities.limitations: Workspaces reshape hints and defaults; they do not change permission modes.

capabilities.name: Pipeline view
capabilities.summary: A run, stage by stage with its files and checks — not one green checkmark.
capabilities.search: pipeline stages run files verification events stage by stage
capabilities.what_it_is: Lists recent runtime runs, then shows a run's recorded stages, files and verification events stage by stage.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A governed run is inspectable stage by stage with its files and verification events, not just a final green check.
capabilities.limitations: Runtime-backed: needs a connected axym-runtime daemon.

capabilities.name: Execution graph
capabilities.summary: See why a run is waiting: stages, gates, agents and dependencies.
capabilities.search: graph dependency tree stage gate agent task waiting
capabilities.what_it_is: Interactive stage, gate, agent and task dependency tree for a runtime run.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Dependencies between stages, gates, agents and tasks are visible, so you can see why a run is waiting.
capabilities.limitations: Runtime-backed: needs a connected axym-runtime daemon.

capabilities.name: Evidence browser
capabilities.summary: Trace any claim to inspected, inferred, verified or failed proof.
capabilities.search: evidence inspected inferred verified failed claim proof trace hash-chained
capabilities.what_it_is: Inspect the evidence primitive behind a claim: inspected, inferred, verified and failed proof.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Claims are traceable to inspected, inferred, verified or failed proof, so you can judge a result on its evidence.
capabilities.limitations: Runtime-backed: needs a connected axym-runtime daemon.

capabilities.name: Health, intelligence & observatory
capabilities.summary: Runtime health, provider cooldowns and active skills, readable in place.
capabilities.search: health intel observatory daemon cooldowns ledger skills active
capabilities.what_it_is: Read the daemon self-report and provider cooldowns, the decision ledger with estimates and measured outcomes, and active skills with evaluation candidates.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Runtime health, measured routing decisions and active skills are readable without leaving the terminal.
capabilities.limitations: Daemon-backed sections need axym-runtime; TUI-local health is always available.

capabilities.name: Handover & Work Passport
capabilities.summary: The next session inherits the brief, criteria and recovery context.
capabilities.search: handover passport handoff brief acceptance criteria recovery export
capabilities.what_it_is: See session state, unresolved tasks and uncommitted work, or show and export the durable passport (product brief, acceptance criteria, execution truth, recovery context).
capabilities.why_it_matters: The next session or person receives the brief, criteria, execution truth and recovery context instead of a blank chat.
capabilities.limitations: The passport is an explicit export, never an automatic transfer of session state.

capabilities.name: Settings, themes & density
capabilities.summary: Graphite, classic or contrast — comfort settings persist.
capabilities.search: settings theme graphite classic contrast density vim verbose header
capabilities.what_it_is: Toggle Vim editing, verbose tool output and a compact header, or switch between graphite, classic and high-contrast themes.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Comfort settings persist, so the terminal fits your screen and reading preference across sessions.
capabilities.limitations: Themes affect the TUI only; each surface keeps its own appearance settings.

capabilities.name: Real mux pane adapters
capabilities.summary: Live panes in tmux, zellij and wezterm — argv-safe launchers, kill-before-close.
capabilities.search: mux pane adapters tmux zellij wezterm psmux tiled wave layout kill before close exec adr-0018
capabilities.what_it_is: A mux viewer contract with a strict pane-ID sanitizer and prober, argv-safe launchers for tmux, zellij and wezterm (psmux runs through the tmux adapter), and a tiled wave layout manager with manual close and kill-before-close semantics (ADR-0018).
capabilities.why_it_matters: Runs can drive real terminal panes in the multiplexer you already use, without unsafe argument handling or orphaned processes.
capabilities.limitations: Requires the named multiplexer installed; without one, runs stay in the TUI's own layout.

capabilities.name: Blast radius & investigation
capabilities.summary: Inspect changed symbols, callers and diagnostics, or trace failure root causes.
capabilities.search: blast radius callers diagnostics investigate failure trace root cause
capabilities.what_it_is: Inspect changed symbols, their callers and compiler diagnostics before approving edits, or run structured failure investigations over execution traces and logs.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You see the downstream impact of an edit or the root cause of a failure before committing.
capabilities.limitations: Blast radius is computed from language-server and compiler data where available; dynamic call paths are not tracked.

capabilities.name: Activity Inspector & receipts
capabilities.summary: Inspect live tool/file transparency and checksummed evidence receipts.
capabilities.search: activity footprint receipt files transparency checksum audit hash-chained
capabilities.what_it_is: Inspect live tool and file transparency (NOW, FILES, SAFETY, OUTCOME, WHY), per-turn file audit records, and harness-authored evidence receipts with verification checksums.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Every file read, write and shell touch is auditable with a verifiable receipt.
capabilities.limitations: Receipts cover harness-recorded actions; actions taken outside the governed tools are not receipted.

capabilities.name: Code intelligence & safety
capabilities.summary: Failure investigations and blast radius, before you approve or roll back.
capabilities.search: investigate blast radius proof scars mcp memory activity footprint goldfish drift
capabilities.what_it_is: The inspection family: /investigate for focused failure analysis, /blast for change impact, /proof for offline evidence verification and /scars for the organisation's recorded rules.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You can answer what broke, what else it touches, and whether the claim is provable — before you approve or roll back.
capabilities.limitations: Investigations read recorded evidence; they observe and explain, they do not certify a repair.

capabilities.name: Code review & QA
capabilities.summary: A second pass for hidden assumptions, weak tests and edge cases.
capabilities.search: review qa code quality assumptions edge cases tests references
capabilities.what_it_is: Runs a code-quality pass for hidden assumptions, simplicity, surgical diffs, edge cases and test completeness, with file and line references.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A second pass finds hidden assumptions and weak tests before they reach your branch, with file and line references.
capabilities.limitations: Review quality depends on the selected provider; independence is labelled, not assumed.

capabilities.name: Security review
capabilities.summary: Threat modelling with evidence-cited findings and a remediation plan.
capabilities.search: security threat model audit vulnerabilities remediation evidence masvs web check posture scan store preflight
capabilities.problem: "Is this safe?" usually gets a vibe-answer — you need threat modelling with cited evidence, and mobile work needs a store-grade pass, not a promise.
capabilities.what_it_is: Threat-models the target, reviews code and configuration with captured evidence, and returns a prioritized remediation plan. On mobile targets, /security --masvs adds an OWASP MASVS-aligned pass and a store preflight gate runs before submission.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Evidence-cited findings turn "is this safe?" into a prioritized, reviewable list, and store submission is gated rather than hoped for.
capabilities.limitations: Web posture scanning runs against URLs you point it at from your machine; MASVS depth on real devices depends on the device bridge connection (T-050 hardware journey partial — see the device bridge entry).

capabilities.name: Background test runner
capabilities.summary: Real test output, without blocking the conversation.
capabilities.search: test runner background real output exit code conversation
capabilities.what_it_is: Runs the project's tests without blocking the conversation and reports the result back into the session.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Tests run without blocking the conversation and the real result comes back into the same session.
capabilities.limitations: The runner reports real exit codes; it does not interpret or paper over failing suites.

capabilities.name: Diff, pull, undo & bisect
capabilities.summary: Every change visible and reversible — down to binary-searching a regression.
capabilities.search: diff pull undo bisect checkpoint stash reversible regression
capabilities.what_it_is: Inspect uncommitted changes with interactive hunk review, pull the remote tracking branch, shelve work into a reversible stash, or binary-search checkpoints for the turn that introduced a regression.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Edits are reversible and reviewable hunk by hunk: inspect changes, pull updates, undo a turn, or binary-search checkpoints to find the regression.
capabilities.limitations: Undo covers Axym-recorded turns; manual edits between turns are outside its checkpoints.

capabilities.name: Reusable workflows
capabilities.summary: Save a sequence once; replay it on any provider.
capabilities.search: workflow reusable sequence named replay provider starter
capabilities.what_it_is: Define a named sequence of prompts once, then replay it on any provider. Four starter workflows cover engineering, product discovery, security review and QA.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A sequence that worked once becomes a repeatable procedure you can run on any provider.
capabilities.limitations: Workflows replay prompts, not tool side effects; each run still passes the gates.

capabilities.name: Project setup
capabilities.summary: One command wires a project into Axym's conventions — never overwriting.
capabilities.search: init project setup starter config axym.yaml desktop shared overwrite
capabilities.what_it_is: Writes a starter .axym.yaml shared with the desktop app, without ever overwriting an existing file.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A project gets a starter config in one command without overwriting the configuration you already wrote.
capabilities.limitations: Refuses to overwrite; existing configuration always wins.

capabilities.name: Proof-carrying races & scars
capabilities.summary: Lock a failing invariant, race solutions in worktrees and verify signed RED→GREEN proofs.
capabilities.search: race proof scars solve verify-proof red green invariant ed25519 worktree speculative shadow evidence golden cassette replay bench reproduce offline
capabilities.problem: "Tests passed" claims are unverifiable after the fact, and speculative work has no way to prove it exercised a real failing baseline.
capabilities.what_it_is: Lock a failing test invariant on HEAD, race candidate implementations in isolated worktrees, verify non-vacuous RED→GREEN proofs with Ed25519 signatures, and enforce organization scar rules that block recurring mistakes. Speculative shadow evidence runs verification while approval gates hold, and offline replay (axym bench --reproduce, the T-048 cassette path) re-checks recorded runs without live CLIs.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Fixes are backed by cryptographic proof against a real failing baseline — never a vacuous pass — and recorded runs can be re-verified offline.
capabilities.use_it: /race · /proof · /scars · axym solve · axym verify-proof · axym bench --reproduce
capabilities.limitations: Race worktree brackets need git; offline replay covers recorded cassette runs only — it cannot conjure evidence for turns that were never recorded.

capabilities.name: Declarative Flow OS
capabilities.summary: Workflows compile to bounded, resumable lockfiles with least-privilege outputs.
capabilities.search: flow os workflow lockfile dag resume least privilege limits capture starter packs publish
capabilities.problem: Trusted multi-step procedures live in people's heads or in fragile shell scripts, with no bound on cost, outputs or resume behaviour.
capabilities.what_it_is: /flow [list|run|resume|status|inspect|capture] runs workflows stored under .axym/workflows. They compile to least-privilege lockfiles with safe-output caps, execute in DAG order under turn, cost and wall-clock limits, resume durably, and capture the session for inspection.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A procedure you trust becomes a bounded, reviewable unit of work instead of a prompt you hope behaves — with role starter packs and signed organisation packs.
capabilities.limitations: Workflows are declarative lockfiles, not arbitrary code; five role starter packs ship, and organisation packs must be signed to publish.

capabilities.name: Bundled skills

capabilities.search: bundled skills po aei product owner engineering intelligence qa reverse
capabilities.what_it_is: Product-Owner Intelligence, Axym Engineering Intelligence, reverse engineering and break-it QA ship inside the binary and work in any project.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Four experts ship inside the binary, so product, engineering, QA and reverse-engineering work is available in every project.
capabilities.limitations: Installed same-name skills take precedence over bundled ones.

capabilities.limitations: Skill format follows SKILL.md conventions; undeclared modes error instead of silently falling back.

capabilities.name: Project configuration
capabilities.summary: One .axym.yaml teaches it your stack, style and forbidden libraries.
capabilities.search: project configuration axym.yaml stack style guide forbidden libraries budgets

capabilities.why_it_matters: One .axym.yaml teaches the agent your stack, style, forbidden libraries and secrets, so it works in your codebase rather than a generic one.

capabilities.name: Plugin trust & lifecycle
capabilities.summary: Scaffold, validate and trust local plugins with fail-closed treeSha256 tamper revocation.
capabilities.search: plugin trust init validate list treesha256 tamper revocation verifier fail-closed
capabilities.what_it_is: Scaffold, validate, trust and list repo-local verifier and command plugins with fail-closed treeSha256 tamper revocation.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Untrusted or modified plugins cannot execute silently in your workspace.
capabilities.limitations: Trust is per-repo and explicit; an untrusted plugin is refused, not sandboxed.

capabilities.name: Living Repo Brain & memory
capabilities.summary: Zero-rescan context pyramid and causal lessons closed-loop from /race.
capabilities.search: memory living repo brain context pyramid ecs import cone co-change causal lessons prompt cache crc32 delta prefix stability e1 telemetry
capabilities.problem: Every turn re-pays to re-orient in a large codebase, and lessons the organisation already learned are forgotten by the next session.
capabilities.what_it_is: A zero-rescan three-layer context pyramid (ECS fingerprints, depth-2 import cone, co-change slice) with causal lessons closed-loop from /race, feeding a stable shared prompt prefix whose cache hit rate is measured — in a repeated ~40k-token prompt, $0.161 cold versus $0.008 warm (91% cached).
capabilities.why_it_matters: Large repositories stay fast and cheap to orient in: the prefix the provider cache exploits is preserved across providers and turns instead of being rebuilt.
capabilities.limitations: Cache figures come from one measured repeated prompt, not a guarantee; staleness is reported by /memory rather than hidden.

capabilities.name: Self-improvement proposals
capabilities.summary: Evidence-gated, reversible tweaks to its own instructions.
capabilities.search: evolve self-improvement proposals statistical gate rollback before-state
capabilities.what_it_is: /evolve [list|accept|dismiss|rollback <id>] reviews proposals that have passed a sequential-probability gate. Accepting updates a target file; rollback restores the pinned before-state.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Improvements to the agent's own instructions are evidence-gated and reversible, not silent edits to behaviour.
capabilities.limitations: Proposals never self-apply; a human accepts, and rollback always exists.

capabilities.name: Council mode
capabilities.summary: One prompt, many providers, one merged answer.
capabilities.search: council parallel providers merge synthesis second opinion borda governed overnight queue quota-reset parking warm handoff e3 e7
capabilities.problem: Getting a genuine second opinion means babysitting two sessions, and overnight work dies when a quota resets at 2am.
capabilities.what_it_is: Runs the same prompt across two or more providers in parallel and merges their answers into one synthesized response; on a governed run, Borda-ranked consensus with anonymous ballots and a decision record. Overnight work parks through quota walls: benched providers resume at their reset time and hand the next provider a ≤2 KB warm delta, and axym queue submits governed work without blocking the terminal.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You get cross-checked answers and a decision record without managing sessions, and work keeps moving across quota resets instead of dying at a 401.
capabilities.limitations: Council needs two or more installed providers; queue submissions still respect human approval gates and never auto-approve.

capabilities.name: Cross-provider verification
capabilities.summary: The reviewer can be a different AI than the author — honestly labelled.
capabilities.search: cross-provider verification independent reviewer author labelled desktop stage
capabilities.what_it_is: Run review or security on a different provider than the coder; the run labels whether the verifier was independent of the code author or shared its provider and model.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Review by a different provider than the author is labelled honestly, so independence is a fact you can check rather than a claim.
capabilities.use_it: Desktop → Expert options → AI system per stage
capabilities.limitations: True independence requires a second installed provider; otherwise the shared-provider label is shown.

capabilities.name: Agent Hub & fleet overview
capabilities.summary: A live roster of every run — attach to the right one instead of guessing.
capabilities.search: agent hub fleet roster capacity active runs oldest failures attach alt+a
capabilities.what_it_is: Toggle a live roster of runtime runs, select and attach to one, or read configured capacity, active runs, oldest in-flight work and recent failures.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A live roster shows what the runtime is doing, so you can attach to the right run instead of guessing.
capabilities.limitations: Runtime-backed: needs a connected axym-runtime daemon.

capabilities.name: Run comparison & stage costs
capabilities.summary: Why one run beat another — commits, configs and per-stage spend.
capabilities.search: compare runs stage costs tokens spend calls commit dependencies config
capabilities.what_it_is: Compare what two runtime runs actually ran against (commit, dependencies, config), and read per-stage token, spend and call-count evidence.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Comparing commit, dependencies, configuration and per-stage spend explains why one run beat another.
capabilities.limitations: Runtime-backed: needs a connected axym-runtime daemon.

capabilities.what_it_is: A LinUCB cost/failover router unifies the keyless cloud CLIs, adds queue arbitrage, and backs decisions with a dated local rate card via the daemon's AXYM_AUTO_ROUTE=cost setting, inside the economic governor's Normal/Restricted/Blocked spend states.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Model choice learns from measured cost and queue data instead of guesses, and the reasoning stays inspectable on your machine.
capabilities.limitations: Requires the axym serve daemon; rate cards are dated local files, not live pricing feeds.

capabilities.name: Headless mode
capabilities.summary: Scripts and CI: JSON output, stable exit codes, same engine.
capabilities.search: headless script ci jsonl exit codes pipeline shell prompt
capabilities.what_it_is: Run one prompt from the shell or stdin with text or JSONL output and stable exit codes for scripts and CI.
capabilities.why_it_matters: The same engine runs in scripts and CI with text or JSONL output and stable exit codes.
capabilities.limitations: Headless turns share the same permission gates; gates that need a human fail closed with a recorded reason.

capabilities.name: Live steering & queueing
capabilities.summary: Change course mid-run at the next safe boundary — or queue guidance.
capabilities.search: steer queue instruction safe boundary interrupt guidance
capabilities.what_it_is: Change course mid-turn at the next safe boundary on the governed runtime, or queue guidance for later without interrupting the run.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You can change course at a safe boundary or queue guidance for later without interrupting a long run.
capabilities.limitations: Steering lands at safe boundaries, not mid-edit; it never bypasses gates.

capabilities.name: Follow, fork & compare runs
capabilities.summary: Attach for live replay, fork an experiment, open a read-only viewer.
capabilities.search: attach follow fork lineage child viewer replay live read-only
capabilities.what_it_is: Attach to a Desktop or Mobile run with durable replay and live updates, fork it into a child lineage, or open a second read-only viewer.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Runs have lineage: attach for live replay, fork a child experiment, or open a read-only viewer.
capabilities.limitations: Runtime-backed: needs a connected axym-runtime daemon.

capabilities.name: Parallel isolated runs
capabilities.summary: Many goals at once — each in its own worktree, merged only by you.
capabilities.search: parallel isolated runs worktree switch integrate apply events staged mux panes tmux zellij wezterm adr-0018 kill-before-close
capabilities.problem: Parallel agents collide on one working tree: staged files mix, events interleave, and a close can orphan live panes.
capabilities.what_it_is: Start several governed pipeline runs in isolated linked worktrees, switch the visible run without mixing events or staged files, and preview or explicitly apply a finished run's worktree integration — with live panes in tmux, zellij or wezterm via argv-safe adapters and kill-before-close semantics (ADR-0018).
capabilities.why_it_matters: Several features progress at once without fighting over one working tree; each run keeps its own events and staged files, integration is a separate explicit decision, and closing never orphans a pane.
capabilities.limitations: Structural worktree creation is gated by AXYM_PERSISTENT_RUNTIME=1 on the daemon (the error is shown verbatim); mux panes need the named multiplexer installed.

capabilities.name: Delegation & worker control
capabilities.summary: Delegate to isolated workers with fencing tokens, acceptance checks and stall recovery.
capabilities.search: delegate workers fencing token recover stall land discard isolated
capabilities.what_it_is: Delegate tasks to isolated workers, inspect fencing tokens and progress, wait for acceptance, land verified work or recover stalled sessions.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Parallel worker delegation stays fenced and recoverable even if a worker stalls.
capabilities.limitations: Stalled workers can be recovered or discarded, but their uncommitted scratch state may be lost by design.

capabilities.name: Shell entry points
capabilities.summary: The whole engine, exposed as non-interactive commands for scripts and CI.
capabilities.search: shell entry points non-interactive scripts ci solve queue ship pr flow aei memory plugin export passport relay team scars verify-proof web bench fitness
capabilities.what_it_is: Everything the interactive TUI can do has a non-interactive form: axym solve, axym queue, axym ship, axym flow, axym verify-proof, axym accounts/files/plugin/memory, axym export-session/passport, axym relay/team, axym scars/pr, axym web — plus the engineering gates (axym fitness --json, axym bench --reproduce) used by the repo's own CI.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Scripts and CI drive the same governed engine, policy and evidence store as the interactive session — no parallel implementation to drift.
capabilities.use_it: axym solve "<goal>" · axym queue · axym ship · axym flow · axym verify-proof
capabilities.limitations: Exit codes are stable (0/1/2/130); gates that need a human fail closed in CI rather than blocking interactively.

capabilities.name: Share & read-only viewing
capabilities.summary: Teammates follow along with zero write authority.

capabilities.what_it_is: Share a session or live run with collaborators; viewers follow an isolated read-only event stream and cannot steer, approve or write.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Collaborators can follow without write authority, so observation never becomes an accidental change.
capabilities.limitations: Viewers see the shared stream only; side conversations stay local to the owner.

capabilities.name: Phone pairing
capabilities.summary: Approve gates and steer from your phone via a QR-paired, revocable link.
capabilities.search: phone remote qr pairing wifi tailscale tunnel pin revocable t-050 cert-pinning web push
capabilities.what_it_is: Continue the live session from a phone over the same Wi-Fi, Tailscale or a Cloudflare tunnel, with a QR pairing card, PIN or scoped access and a revocable link.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A QR code and scoped link let you approve or steer from a phone while the session stays on your workstation.
capabilities.limitations: T-050 real-phone journey is partial: Wi-Fi cert-pinning and closed-app Web Push delivery are not yet certified — treat mobile connectivity and the TLS preview as experimental until the release notes mark them GA.

capabilities.name: Browser bridge
capabilities.summary: A PIN-protected web surface over the governed runtime.
capabilities.search: browser bridge web page pin token watch approval mobile friendly
capabilities.what_it_is: Serve a phone-friendly page over the governed runtime with live transcript, submit, steer, cancel and approval actions, protected by a PIN or token.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A PIN-protected page gives a phone-sized approval surface over the governed runtime without moving the session.
capabilities.limitations: Shares the T-050 experimental status: cert-pinned Wi-Fi and closed-app push are not yet certified; keep the bridge on a trusted network.

capabilities.name: Detach and attach
capabilities.summary: Close the laptop; the work continues. Reattach from anywhere.
capabilities.search: detach attach ssh close terminal keep running redraw size
capabilities.what_it_is: Free the terminal while the session keeps running, then return from any terminal or SSH login with the transcript redrawn at the new size.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Close the terminal or lose SSH and the work continues; reattach from anywhere with the transcript redrawn at that size.
capabilities.limitations: The session lives on the machine that started it; attaching happens there, not from another host.

capabilities.name: Push notifications
capabilities.summary: Told when a turn finishes, fails or stalls — stop polling the terminal.
capabilities.search: notify push notification ntfy turn finished failed cooling topic self-hosted
capabilities.what_it_is: Send a push when a turn finishes, fails, or every provider is cooling, through ntfy.sh or a self-hosted topic.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Long runs tell you when they finish, fail or stall, so you are not polling a terminal for news.
capabilities.limitations: Delivery uses ntfy or a self-hosted topic; closed-app Web Push on iOS is part of the uncertified T-050 hardware journey.

capabilities.name: Session & run handoff
capabilities.summary: Move work between machines with explicit offer, accept and retract steps.
capabilities.search: handoff session run checkpoint export import offer accept retract machine
capabilities.what_it_is: Export or import a session, or move a multi-machine run checkpoint with offer, export, accept, status and retract actions.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Work moves between surfaces and machines with explicit offer, accept and retract steps instead of copy-pasted state.
capabilities.limitations: Handoff moves explicit checkpoints; unrecorded scratch state is not transferred.

capabilities.name: Mobile developer platform (iOS & Android)
capabilities.summary: Simulators, journeys, screenshots and design diffs — store-grade mobile QA from the terminal.
capabilities.search: device bridge mobile simulator journey screenshot design diff pair termcaps ios android maestro masvs bg background passport proof visual axym/mobile.json
capabilities.problem: Mobile verification means manual simulator dances and "it looked fine on my device" claims that no one can inspect later.
capabilities.what_it_is: A device platform driven from the terminal: /devices and /device inventory simulators and connected hardware with a unified driver, /sim drives a simulator session, /mobile runs multi-turn journeys with crash/ANR harvesting, /mobile-proof captures screenshot, hierarchy and schema-v2 visual diff evidence, /qa --maestro adds Maestro store-grade QA and /security --masvs the MASVS pass, while /bg keeps work running in the background and axym doctor --mobile reports readiness.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A visual change is proven with captures and a design diff — not a claim — and store submission is gated, not hoped for.
capabilities.limitations: Certified today on iOS/Android simulators; the real-phone journey (cert-pinned Wi-Fi, closed-app push, physical-device visual diff fidelity) is partial under T-050 and stated as experimental, not GA.

capabilities.name: Team collaboration
capabilities.summary: Team keys, shared templates and encrypted relay messages.
capabilities.search: team peers relay signing keys templates profiles encrypted deployments
capabilities.what_it_is: /team [status|key|peers|templates|profiles|deployments|settings], /peers and /relay <message> manage team signing keys, discover peers, share templates, profiles and settings, and send encrypted relay messages.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A team can share working conventions and coordinate across sessions without moving the run or handing out blanket write authority.
capabilities.limitations: Relay is message-scoped; it never grants write authority to another member's session.

capabilities.name: Governed runtime connection
capabilities.summary: Durable runs, evidence and approvals in a daemon — the TUI is the control surface.
capabilities.search: runtime daemon durable runs evidence approvals replay control surface serve
capabilities.what_it_is: Use axym-runtime for durable runs, evidence, approvals, fleet views and run replay while keeping the same terminal interface.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Durable runs, evidence and approvals live in the runtime, so long work survives terminal restarts.
capabilities.limitations: Daemon-backed features degrade to local-session behaviour when no runtime is connected; the error is shown, not hidden.

capabilities.name: /ship governed pipeline
capabilities.summary: One command runs the full governed pipeline — nothing reaches the repo without an explicit, reversible apply.
capabilities.search: ship governed pipeline plan design code security review qa apply staging checkpoint undo approve revise reject hash-chained receipts result ledger po
capabilities.problem: A fuzzy request usually goes straight to an edit; you want it scoped, staged, verified and reversible before it touches the repo.
capabilities.what_it_is: /ship "<goal>" (with /po scoping up front) submits a plan → design → code → security → review → qa run to the axym serve daemon with journaled human gate decisions (/approve, /revise, /reject, /cancel). Changes stage in .axym/edit-staging/run-<id> and reach your project only through /ship apply, which is checkpointed so /undo covers it. Speculative shadow evidence is gathered while gates hold, and each closed run leaves a hash-chained verification receipt trail.
capabilities.why_it_matters: The whole governed pipeline is one command, and nothing touches your project without an explicit, reversible apply — with receipts you can re-verify offline.
capabilities.limitations: Requires the axym serve daemon; hash-chained receipts record what ran — they certify verification, not product correctness.

capabilities.name: Laya decisions & vibe mode
capabilities.summary: Low-risk calls get classified and recorded, not asked. Ask for the smallest honest pipeline.
capabilities.search: laya vibe decisions classify low-risk announce record smallest honest pipeline
capabilities.what_it_is: Classify low-risk decisions, announce and record them, or ask the runtime for the smallest honest pipeline it can justify.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Low-risk decisions are classified and recorded, and you can ask for the smallest honest pipeline instead of a default heavy one.
capabilities.limitations: /vibe may decline with a reason; it never silently downgrades a governed run.

capabilities.name: Provider priority
capabilities.summary: See exactly how the default provider was chosen — failover stops being mysterious.
capabilities.search: priority resolution order default provider environment config manifest
capabilities.what_it_is: Show how the default provider was resolved across environment variables, config and provider manifests.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You can see exactly how the default provider was chosen, which makes failover predictable instead of mysterious.
capabilities.limitations: Priority explains the resolution; changing it is a config change, not a runtime override.

capabilities.name: Self-update with checksums
capabilities.summary: Updates verify SHA-256 before touching the binary, and install atomically.
capabilities.search: update self checksum sha-256 atomic channel asset verify
capabilities.what_it_is: Checks the release channel, downloads the platform asset, verifies its SHA-256 against SHA256SUMS.txt and installs atomically.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Updates verify SHA-256 before installing atomically, so a corrupted or substituted asset cannot be silently installed.
capabilities.limitations: Update channels point at published GitHub releases only; unsigned or third-party channels are refused.

capabilities.name: Keep-awake during long runs
capabilities.summary: Idle sleep cannot suspend a long run — released the moment the turn ends.
capabilities.search: keep awake power assertion idle sleep suspend opt out
capabilities.what_it_is: Holds a power assertion while a turn runs so idle sleep cannot suspend the work; opt out with a marker file.
capabilities.why_it_matters: Idle sleep cannot suspend long work; the assertion is released when the turn ends and can be opted out.
capabilities.limitations: Applies to OS idle sleep; explicit shutdowns or battery-kill policies still interrupt work.

capabilities.name: Atomic local state
capabilities.summary: A crash cannot leave half-written sessions or history.
capabilities.search: atomic state fsync rename temp file crash half-written sessions history
capabilities.what_it_is: Sessions, history and allow-lists are written with a temp-file, fsync and rename sequence, so a crash cannot leave half-written state.
capabilities.why_it_matters: A crash cannot leave half-written sessions, history or allow-lists because writes use a temp-file, fsync and rename sequence.
capabilities.limitations: Atomicity covers completed writes; an in-flight write at the exact crash moment falls back to the last good state.

capabilities.name: AIDE run diagnosis
capabilities.summary: Inspect a misbehaving run — events, integrity, replay — without destroying it.
capabilities.search: debug aide diagnosis event integrity replay inspect pause resume evidence sentinel adversarial fitness require-context ci gate
capabilities.problem: When a run misbehaves, the usual fix is to kill it and lose the evidence — you need adversarial inspection and a CI gate that refuses vacuous passes.
capabilities.what_it_is: On a connected runtime run, inspect failure evidence, event integrity, bounded pipeline replay and run-scoped effect counts; pause, investigate or resume diagnosis while retaining the original run and its permissions. The same evidence discipline backs the headless axym fitness [--json] [--require-context] gate, which exits non-zero on a blocker and treats an absent context as a failure — never a vacuous pass.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You can interrogate a misbehaving run without destroying it, and CI can require real, present evidence instead of trusting a green check.
capabilities.limitations: Observations do not certify a repair — retest stays a separate, explicit step; the fitness gate needs the committed engineering context (.axym/engineering/architecture.json) to be present.

capabilities.name: Zero-trust MCP firewall
capabilities.summary: Local stdio/HTTP MCP firewall with capability-lattice admission and taint tracking.
capabilities.search: mcp firewall capability lattice taint stdio http audited tool zero-trust delegated read edit write grep
capabilities.problem: MCP tools run with whatever power your session has — a hostile or over-scoped server can read, write or exfiltrate far beyond its job.
capabilities.what_it_is: A local MCP stdio/HTTP firewall with scoped capability-lattice admission and untrusted-output tainting; delegated file tools (Read/Edit/Write/Grep) stay behind the audited route, and /mcp shows tool scopes plus the admission ledger.
capabilities.why_it_matters: External MCP tools operate under least privilege with every call audited — untrusted output is tainted, not trusted because a tool produced it.
capabilities.limitations: The firewall governs MCP traffic through Axym; tools configured inside another CLI's own MCP setup are outside this boundary.

capabilities.name: Governed run controls
capabilities.summary: One inbox for every decision; drift review before anything ships.
capabilities.search: inbox mission preview goldfish revise cancel drift decision elephant review quota-reset parking warm handoff
capabilities.what_it_is: The human-loop controls for governed runs: /inbox collects approvals, revisions and rejections across gates into one queue; /mission shows the objective and constraints; /preview shows the proposed plan with per-provider badges before execution; /goldfish reviews drift between the agreed spec and the produced change; /revise reopens a run with new instructions and /cancel stops it with the reason recorded.
capabilities.why_it_matters: You decide from a single queue instead of hunting through transcripts, and drift is reviewed before anything ships rather than discovered after.
capabilities.limitations: Runtime-backed decisions queue in the daemon; without axym-runtime the inbox covers local gates only.
